text:
Maria: Heads-up — after the deploy to main yesterday I'm seeing a perf regression on 8xA100 MoE runs. latency tail spikes on long sequences, looks like token routing bursts. attaching profiler: https://perf.redwood/internal/trace/1767504321 :disappointed:
Jon: thx. rough numbers?
Maria: p95 generation increased from 120ms -> 220ms for 4k tokens per request across batch size 8. flame shows fat all-to-all steps during routing phases, and a surprising kernel fallback to tf32 GEMM on some shards.
Kevin: hmm. can you paste the kernel selection log? i suspect the kernel selector is picking a fallback because workspace estimation is off.
Maria: here's snippet from runtime logs:
```
[kernel-selector] model=moe_v2, layer=expert_mlp_12, chosen_kernel=fp16_gemm_amp, fallback=tf32_gemm (reason=workspace_limit)
[routing] all_to_all: 128.42ms, comm_wait: 90.10ms, compute: 28.32ms
[kvcache] cache_hit_rate=0.87, eviction=0.13, prefetch_misses=0.04
```
Sree: eviction 13% seems high for steady-state. are we flushing KV before routing? last change to the KV prefetch policy was the batching heuristics tweak.
Jon: right — we recently pushed dynamic-batch window shrinker which collapses short sequences to the front of the batch. That reduced latency for small seqs but may increase fragmentation for long sequences that need KV offsets.
Kevin: also saw that the kernel selector ties workspace to per-GPU freeram estimate which undercounts when NCCL buffers inflate during all-reduce. so selector thinks it must choose smaller workspace -> picks slower tf32_gemm. that plus all-to-all stalls explains tail.
perf-bot: Automated flame summary (trace=1767504321): top 3 offenders: 1) all_to_all (41% cpu wall), 2) kernel_fallback_gemm (29%), 3) kv_eviction_gc (12%). Suggested actions: re-evaluate kernel workspace budget; add pre-route KV pinning; overlap all-to-all with local expert compute where possible.
Maria: nice. any quick mitigation we can try on prod to reduce tail right now? can we force kernel=fp16_gemm_amp via env for that model? @Jon
Jon: yes we can add REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=fp16_gemm_amp for that model id, but it's risky if workspace actually insufficient -> OOM. safer: increase per-GPU workspace budget by +256MB and enable NCCL_BUFFERS=SIZED to cap NCCL memory footprint.
Sree: i can do a staged change: 1) enable NCCL buffer cap on a few instances, 2) bump kernel workspace on same canary, 3) enable a KV prefetch pin for long-seq route. will run rollouts in canary group.
Kevin: also propose scheduler tweak: when routing is active, try to start local expert compute for top-k experts before issuing all-to-all for remaining tokens (overlap). may require changing op ordering in runtime.
Maria: put a short checklist so we can track:
- [ ] canary NCCL buffer cap (Sree)
- [ ] bump kernel workspace + force kernel in canary (Jon)
- [ ] KV prefetch pin for long seqs (Sree)
- [ ] runtime op scheduler change PR (Kevin)
- [ ] post-change profilers + perf-bot trace (Maria)
Jon: i'll open the kernel workspace PR and a canary rollout. PR: https://git.redwood/r/kr/3234
Sree: started canary job: job/1767504337, will ping when stable.
Maria: thanks — after canary report we'll decide urgent rollback vs gradual fix. anyone see other angles? :thinking_face:
Kevin: long-term: kernel selector should estimate NCCL buffer hold and per-request KV reservation. putting that into estimator will avoid safe-but-slower fallbacks.
perf-bot: Note: if you need a flame diff between builds run `perfctl diff --base=main~1 --head=main --trace=1767504321` and post result.
Maria: copying logs into infra ticket: https://issues.redwood/INF-1192
Jon: ack. will follow up with stats in ~30m.
Maria: thanks all :thumbsup:
